terra.problem: Being sold for a pair of sandals does not establish that the person was treated as worth less than a pair.
The passage mentions garments taken in pledge, but it does not say a cloak comes up.
The joke about not getting a whole outfit makes light of the charge that needy people were sold.
The text says the wine was obtained through fines; it does not say money was squeezed out of people or used to pay for it.
The text does not say nobody gave the wine freely.
Calling it 'not a good deal' adds a detail about the transaction that the text does not give.
The explanation is generic and merely repeats the answer without adding a meaningful explanation.
The claim that seventy appears elsewhere in the Bible needs a reference.
Being commanded not to prophesy does not establish that the prophets were unable to continue.
The text does not say the swift were counting on racing away.
The explanation is flat and repeats the answer without developing what the verse says.
The horseman not saving his life does not establish that nobody has a ride out.
The text says the horseman will not save his life, not that he cannot make it out or that speed does not help him at all.
Fleeing naked does not establish that the man has nothing on him.
Fleeing naked does not establish that the men run with nothing.
The passage says the archer will not stand his ground; 'Nobody holds the line' extends that claim to everyone.
